statement: The trace of an n × n square matrix A, denoted tr(A), is defined as the sum of the elements on its main diagonal: tr(A) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} a_{ii} = a_{11} + a_{22} + \dots + a_{nn}, where a_{ii} denotes the entry on the i-th row and i-th column of A. The supplied sources define the trace directly as a primitive matrix operation and genuinely contain no derivation of the trace itself.

symbols.meaning: square matrix (or m × n matrix in product identities)
entry on the i-th row and i-th column along the main diagonal of matrix A
dimension (number of rows and columns) of square matrix A
matrix compatible with A for addition or multiplication
i-th eigenvalue of matrix A counted with algebraic multiplicity

properties.property: The trace is a linear mapping: tr(A + B) = tr(A) + tr(B) and tr(cA) = c tr(A) for all square matrices A, B and all scalars c.
properties.why: Follows directly from the linearity of entry-wise diagonal summation

properties.property: A matrix and its transpose have identical trace: tr(A) = tr(A^T).
properties.why: Transposition does not alter elements along the main diagonal

properties.property: Trace of a product / Frobenius inner product: tr(A^T B) = tr(A B^T) = tr(B^T A) = tr(B A^T) = \sum_{i=1}^m \sum_{j=1}^n a_{ij} b_{ij} for m × n matrices A and B.
properties.why: The trace of the product equals the sum of all entry-wise products of their elements

properties.property: Commutativity under trace: tr(AB) = tr(BA) for any m × n matrix A and n × m matrix B.
properties.why: Both expressions evaluate to the symmetric sum of entry-wise products \sum_{i=1}^m \sum_{j=1}^n a_{ij} b_{ij}

properties.property: Cyclic property: tr(ABC) = tr(BCA) = tr(CAB) for matrices of compatible dimensions.
properties.why: The trace is invariant under circular shifts of matrix factors

properties.property: Similarity invariance: tr(P^{-1}AP) = tr(A) for any square matrix A and any invertible matrix P of the same dimensions.
properties.why: Consequence of the cyclic property: tr(P^{-1}(AP)) = tr((AP)P^{-1}) = tr(A)

properties.property: Trace of a Kronecker product: tr(A \otimes B) = tr(A) tr(B).
properties.why: Diagonal elements of the Kronecker product are pairwise products of diagonal entries of A and B

properties.property: Trace equals the sum of eigenvalues: tr(A) = \sum_{i=1}^n \lambda_i, where \lambda_i are the eigenvalues of A counted with algebraic multiplicity.
properties.why: A is similar to its Jordan form with eigenvalues on the main diagonal, combined with similarity invariance

properties.property: Trace of commutator vanishes: tr([A, B]) = tr(AB - BA) = 0 for all n × n matrices A and B.
properties.why: Follows from commutativity tr(AB) = tr(BA) combined with linearity

assumptions.assumption: Matrix A must be square (n × n)
assumptions.breaks_when: A is non-square (m × n with m \neq n), where trace is undefined

assumptions.assumption: Matrices in sum tr(A + B) must have identical square dimensions
assumptions.breaks_when: Dimensions of A and B differ or are non-square

assumptions.assumption: In product traces tr(AB), inner dimensions must match such that AB and BA are square
assumptions.breaks_when: Matrix dimensions are incompatible for multiplication or yield non-square products

assumptions.assumption: The transformation matrix P in similarity invariance must be invertible

failure_modes.cause: The trace is strictly defined only for square matrices; non-square matrices do not possess a main diagonal in the required sense
Assuming trace invariance under arbitrary permutations rather than strictly cyclic permutations; arbitrary permutations fail in general unless the matrices are symmetric
Incorrectly treating trace as a multiplicative map; trace distributes across matrix sums, not matrix products

canon_notes: canon expects a derivation but no source performs one, so trace_identities is recorded as a definition
